The command that follows, “You shall not take a wife” (web:Jer.16.2), opens on לֹֽא תִקַּ֥ח לְךָ֖ אִשָּׁ֑ה (oshb:Jer.16.2, byte tier), its own koh-amar rationale running from 16:3 through 16:4. A second command in the same voice follows without a scene change: “Don't enter into the house of mourning” (web:Jer.16.5) carries its koh-amar formula in the same verse as the prohibition itself, כִּֽי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אַל תָּבוֹא֙ בֵּ֣ית מַרְזֵ֔חַ (oshb:Jer.16.5, byte tier), with 16:6-7 running on as that command's rationale and carrying no formula of its own. A third command, “You shall not go into the house of feasting” (web:Jer.16.8), closes with the full divine-name stack “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel says”, כִּי֩ כֹ֨ה אָמַ֜ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.16.9, byte tier). The three prohibitions stay one row because the second-person-singular addressee of the commands at 16:2, 16:5 and 16:8 never changes; the second-person-plural at לְעֵינֵיכֶ֖ם וּבִֽימֵיכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.16.9, byte tier) sits inside the quoted oracle content, addressing the people the oracle describes rather than marking a fresh frame addressee, and each koh-amar onset explains the command just given rather than opening a new frame-owner.
